messages:
Nora Lee: spotting ~0.6% token shortfall in yesterday's invoice-preview vs the ledger commit counts for a set of high-volume tenants (mostly NA). Ledger shows fewer token commits than metering events. sample diff: metering=12,345,678 tokens vs ledger=12,267,891 tokens.

Carlos Mendes: that gap is big. first guess: producer retries + at-least-once vs ledger idempotency mismatch? any errors in producer/ledger logs?

Nora Lee: pasted quick grep from the ingest node logs around the time window:
```
2026-03-21T19:02:11Z INFO metering emit event id=evt_9x... tokens=1024 tenant=na-900
2026-03-21T19:02:11Z ERROR ledger commit failed id=evt_9x... error=504 write timeout
2026-03-21T19:02:12Z WARN metering retrying write id=evt_9x...
2026-03-21T19:02:15Z INFO producer ack received id=evt_9x...
```
looks like producer acks after retry but ledger commit may have raced TTL/dedup window and been dropped by the ledger consumer.

Priya Reddy: TLDR: we may be losing the commit during the ingest->ledger handoff if the ledger consumer applies an idempotency window that expired between initial attempt and retry. If the producer got acked but the ledger consumer already de-duped and discarded the late retry, we get an event with no final ledger_row.

Tom Schultz: do we have the event_id propagated down all the way through the pipeline? without a global GUID we can't correlate metering emit -> producer ack -> ledger row.

Nora Lee: yes event_id exists, but we don't expose it on the invoice-preview side. current preview sums by tenant+route but doesn't check ledger_row existence. want to avoid customer-facing churn so we should show both counts.

Carlos Mendes: proposal: introduce a shadow-write path where ingest writes a lightweight ledger-checkpoint record synchronously (small, <200B) before emitting metering event. the real ledger commit can still be async, but the checkpoint gives us a durable trace to compare. downside: extra sync write on hot path.

Priya Reddy: alternative: keep async flow but extend ledger consumer dedupe window to tolerate 10s of retries. risky for duplication. we should also emit a "write_status" metric per-event: write_status={pending, committed, failed}. then dashboard can show commit_rate per-tenant.

Tom Schultz: runtime perf impact? shadow-write will add p99 ~+6ms on ingest if we use existing fast kv store (redis-like). acceptable for most, but Dedicated low-latency customers might object. we could gate shadow-write behind a config flag per-tenant (default off) and enable for tenants where preview delta > X%.

Nora Lee: agreed. UX for billing team: show a "ledger_committed" line in invoice-preview and mark rows where commit missing as "Orphaned". billing-bot: will that break accounting rules?

billing-bot: note: Orphaned tokens must not be invoiced until reconciled. Please file PLAT-5307 and tag Billing for manual review if orphaned > 1000 tokens per tenant/day.

ingest-bot: alert: ledger_commit_failure_rate spike detected (ingest-prod, region=us-east-1) 2026-03-21T18:50-20:00 UTC. created ticket PLAT-5307.

Carlos Mendes: engineering plan I'd propose: 
1) short-term (hotfix): add write_status metric + dashboard card in staging showing metering_emitted vs ledger_committed by tenant for last 24h. implement minimal on-call alert when committed_rate < 99% for > 15m.
2) mid-term: add optional shadow-write (config per-tenant) to fast KV to get durable checkpoint before emit. fallback to tagging event as "orphaned_candidate" if shadow-write fails.
3) long-term: evaluate increasing dedupe window or redesign ledger idempotency semantics to correlate retries.

Priya Reddy: I'll own short-term metrics + dashboard. can we add a staging card that compares sums and shows DeltaPct and top-10 tenants by delta?

Tom Schultz: I'll prototype shadow-write to redis-cluster and measure p99 impact in staging. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/ingest/pulls/2345 (WIP).

Nora Lee: test plan for short-term: enable metric in staging, run a synthetic replay with injected latency to simulate 5-30s ledger commit delay and verify dashboard surfaces the orphaned spikes.

Carlos Mendes: canary plan for shadow-write: 0.5% of traffic first, measure p99 latency change and committed_rate delta over 48h. rollback if p99 increase > 15ms or committed_rate no improvement.

ingest-bot: update: PLAT-5307 assigned to Nora Lee, priority=P2.

Nora Lee: thanks. follow-ups: Priya->dashboard + alert rules, Tom->shadow-write perf data + PR, Carlos->coordinate canary gating and SLO masks, Billing->confirm reconciliation thresholds. will sync tomorrow 10:30 PT. :calendar:
